# 3 · Research Question

## 3.1 In one sentence: what does this study answer?

Which meeting conditions separate a proposal that is taken up later from one that is not? [stated, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]

## 3.2 What would a well-informed person answer intuitively, and why is that not enough?

Junior members are said to speak less often, and that count is read as the whole story. [stated]

## 3.3 How does answering it move the puzzle forward?

The answer would show whether meeting practices, rather than member dispositions, explain uptake. [proposed, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]

# 4 · Theoretical Constructs and Relationships

## 4.1 What are the core concepts, and where does each definition come from?

Speaking frequency is counted per meeting and not weighted by turn length. [stated, src: glossary.md#speaking-frequency]
Felt safety and speaking frequency can move in opposite directions. [proposed, src: glossary.md#felt-safety, src: glossary.md#speaking-frequency]
Dissent is an utterance, not a count of turns. [proposed, src: glossary.md#dissent]

## 4.2 How do they relate — and is that relationship given in advance or emerging from the material?

A count of turns does not establish that anyone disagreed. [proposed, src: glossary.md#speaking-frequency, src: glossary.md#dissent]
An utterance that disagrees does not establish that a proposal was taken up. [proposed, src: glossary.md#dissent, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]

## 4.3 What mechanism explains the relationship?

Uptake may be a property of the chairing style rather than of the proposal itself. [proposed, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]

## 7.1 What does the material show — separated from what you make of it?

In two meetings a proposal returned as a topic of work weeks later. [stated, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]

# 8 · Contributions

## 8.1 What does the field know now that it did not before?

Turn counts alone do not settle whether a group heard its junior members. [proposed, src: glossary.md#speaking-frequency]

## 8.2 Which assumption in prior work does this change, and how?

Uptake is a property of meetings, not only of individual speakers. [proposed, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]

## 8.3 What follows for practice?

Chairs can watch what happens to a proposal after the meeting ends. [stated, src: glossary.md#proposal-uptake]
